nodes.label: Past, Present and Future on the Constraint Tree
nodes.rationale: Treated as independent the three parts overcount by 130 % — 33 × 4 × 17 = 2,244 against |Λ| = 976, a defect of 1,268 — and conditioning on the transfer separates them exactly. But every two-sided cut (ℓ, q, f, g) gives defect zero, so the tree does the work and q is distinguished only by which two things it separates.

nodes.label: The Four Two-Sided Cuts of the Caterpillar
nodes.rationale: Deleting a coordinate splits the constraint graph precisely when that coordinate is an internal degree-two vertex; n, e and 2S are leaves and k has degree three, so ℓ, q, f, g are the only two-sided cuts that exist.

nodes.label: The Tick Decomposition (k−q) + (q−g)
nodes.rationale: Irreversibility has two independent sources contributing identically — something not removed (350 cells) and something removed but not placed (350), 80 in both — and the split table is its own transpose, so the index weights a choice not taken and a capacity that could not receive the same.

nodes.label: Pauli as a 10.3 % Minority in the Arrow
Future Conditionally Independent of Past Given Present
nodes.rationale: None of the 97 (past, present) pairs determines a single future; for each value of the present every past gives the same future set, the future sets nesting up 5 ⊂ 10 ⊂ 15 ⊂ 17 while the past sets nest down 33 ⊇ 33 ⊇ 23 ⊇ 8. The past constrains only which presents are reachable, and having spent that it has spent everything.
